points.title: Scripting language
points.must: Definition: high-level, interpreted, automates tasks / adds behaviour; runs inside a host (browser, server); examples JavaScript, PHP.
points.model: Scripting language = high-level, usually interpreted language used to automate tasks and add behaviour to applications and web pages. The script runs line by line in an interpreter inside a host program (browser → JavaScript, web server → PHP).

points.title: Interpreted vs compiled
points.must: At least three differences: line by line while running vs whole program before; source code distributed; errors found when the line is reached; slower but quick to edit.
points.model: Compiled: whole program translated before running, executable distributed, all syntax errors at compile time, faster. Interpreted script: translated line by line while running, source code distributed (JS visible), error found only when that line is reached, slower, edit → run immediately.

points.title: Client-side script
points.must: Definition + runs in browser, code visible, can be switched off; uses: interactivity, instant validation; JavaScript in <script>.
points.model: Client-side script = downloaded with the page and run by the user's browser (JavaScript, in <script>…</script>). + instant response, less server load. − code visible, can be disabled/edited → cannot be trusted. Uses: interactivity, instant validation, changing the page without reloading.

points.title: Server-side script
points.must: Definition + runs on web server, user receives only HTML, can access database; PHP in <?php ?>, file .php.
points.model: Server-side script = runs on the web server before the page is sent (PHP between <?php and ?>, file .php). User receives only the resulting HTML. + secure, can use the database, works without JS. − every action needs a request to the server. Uses: form processing, logins, database access.

points.title: Request–response steps
points.must: The numbered flow: request → PHP runs and queries DB → rows returned → HTML sent → JavaScript reacts in browser.
points.model: 1 browser requests marks.php → 2 server runs PHP, sends SQL to database → 3 database returns rows → 4 PHP builds HTML and sends HTML+CSS+JS (no PHP code) → 5 JavaScript reacts to clicks/typing in the browser without the server.

points.title: Choosing client or server (canteen example)
points.must: Rule: instant → client; trusted / needs database → server; validation on both; with at least two examples.
points.model: Running total shown as dishes ticked → client (JS). Empty ID check → both. Prices from database → server (otherwise the user could edit the price). Saving the order → server (PHP + SQL). Rule: instant → client, trusted or database → server.

points.title: Variable and constant
points.must: Definitions; JS let/const, PHP $name; dynamic typing.
points.model: Variable = named memory location whose value can change (identifier, value, data type). Constant = named value that cannot change (const VAT_RATE = 0.12;) → no magic numbers, change in one place. JS: let age = 16; PHP: $age = 16; Both dynamically typed.

points.title: Data types
points.must: Integer, real, string, Boolean, array with examples and JS/PHP names.
points.model: Integer 16 (JS number, PHP int); real 7.5 (number / float); string "Aliya"; Boolean true/false; array [7, 9, 4]; no value: undefined/null (JS), null (PHP).

points.title: Input and output
points.must: JS: prompt, element.value; alert, console.log, textContent. PHP: $_POST/$_GET; echo. Concatenation + vs .
points.model: Input: JS prompt("Age:") or document.getElementById("age").value; PHP $_POST["age"] / $_GET["age"]. Output: JS alert(), console.log(), el.textContent = …; PHP echo. Join: JS "Total: " + total; PHP "Total: " . $total.

points.title: Input is a string
points.must: "5" + "3" = "53"; convert with Number/parseInt/parseFloat; NaN; worked fuel example.
points.model: prompt() and form fields return strings. "5" + "3" = "53" (+ joins strings). Fix: Number(a) + Number(b) = 8; parseInt, parseFloat. Number("abc") = NaN. Fuel: 350 km, 8 l/100 km → 28 l × 270 ₸ = 7560 ₸.

points.title: Selection and condition
points.must: Definitions of selection and condition; if/else if/else syntax in JS and PHP (elseif).
points.model: Selection = structure that chooses which statements to run depending on whether a condition is true or false (if, else if/elseif, else, switch). Condition = Boolean expression (true/false). JS: if (mark >= 50) {…} else if (…) {…} else {…}; PHP: if ($mark >= 50) {…} elseif (…) {…} else {…}.

points.title: Comparison and logical operators
points.model: = assigns, == compares value, === compares value and type ("5" == 5 true, "5" === 5 false). != !== < > <= >=. AND &&, OR ||, NOT !. Range: age >= 14 && age <= 18 (not 14 <= age <= 18).

points.title: Multi-way IF: order matters
points.must: First true condition wins; test highest boundary first; PHP grade example.
points.model: Conditions tested top to bottom, only the first true branch runs. Grades: if ($mark >= 90) A; elseif ($mark >= 75) B; elseif ($mark >= 50) C; else Fail. Mark 78 → B. If >= 50 came first, 95 would get C.

points.title: switch
points.must: Syntax with case, break, default; fall-through; when to use vs if.
points.model: switch (day) { case "Sat": case "Sun": message = "Weekend"; break; default: message = "School day"; } Use for equality with fixed values; if…else if for ranges/AND/OR. Forgotten break → fall-through.

points.title: Cinema ticket worked example
points.must: Multi-way if for age + separate if for Wednesday; traced results.
points.model: age < 7 → 0; else if age <= 17 → 1200; else 2000; then separate if (day === "Wed") price = price / 2. 12, Wed → 600; 30, Wed → 1000; 5, Mon → 0.
